description: Create AI lifestyle product photos from one plain image. Place the item in a room, table or cafe scene so shoppers picture using it without a shoot.

steps_h2: How to Put Your Product in a Scene
steps_lead: The tote you already shot is enough.

steps.d: Use a photo where the bag's straps and base are both visible.
Ask for a cafe table, or a market stall. One nearby object, such as a cup, is enough to show use.
Check the straps against the white photo, then keep the square. Put the price on it yourself.

faq.q: What is a lifestyle product photo?
faq.a: A lifestyle product photo shows the item in a place a buyer recognizes, made from the catalog photo you already have. A mug on a breakfast table is one example.

faq.q: How does the scene get built?
faq.a: Use the catalog photo as the reference, name a place such as a breakfast table, and download the square when the handle still matches.

faq.q: Can a store publish these scenes?
faq.a: Yes. A mug shop can put the breakfast-table square on the product page. Add the price yourself.

faq.q: Can I lock one exact background?
faq.a: You can name the kind of place, such as a cafe table, and change the scene after. The product photo stays the reference.

faq.q: What can I still change once the scene exists?
faq.a: You can change the surface or run a second scene from the same mug. A store's software can request one through the API.

faq.q: Can I try another place after the first result?
faq.a: Yes. Start again with a different surface or one extra object. Each photo is 24 credits.

faq.q: Does the scene replace my plain product photo?
faq.a: No. Keep the original for small details. Use the scene when you want shoppers to picture where the item belongs.

faq.q: How is this different from a photoshoot?
faq.a: A shoot needs a place, a few extra objects, and a day on the calendar. Here you start from a photo you already have. If that photo is hard to read, start with [how to take product photos for AI](page:guide-product-photo-tips).

faq.q: Can I use the scene on a Shopify store?
faq.a: Yes. Download the square and upload it on the product page yourself.

faq.q: Can I post the scene on Instagram?
faq.a: Yes. The square works as the product photo in the feed. Write the caption in Instagram, and add any price in your own editor.

faq.q: Can I post the scene in a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. Finish the headline and the offer in your ad editor. The photo does not include your price.

items.t: Fix Lighting, Clutter, and Image Size
items.d: A stray spoon beside the mug can go. Then fit the file to the slot the store asks for.

items.t: Show Products on an AI Model
items.d: A tote can sit on a shoulder so the buyer sees the drop. That person is an AI model.

items.t: Download a Store-Ready Square
items.d: Download the file and put it where you sell. The price is still something you add.

items.t: Improve Product Photo Lighting and Color
items.d: If the white-background mug looks gray, even out the color before you build a scene on top of it.

items.t: Resize Product Photos for Each Placement
items.d: A story slot and a banner need different shapes; the mug photo can match the placement.

items.t: Request Product Scenes Through an API
items.d: Connect through the API and request a scene for a product already on the list.

items.t: Add Text to Product Photos
items.d: The mug's name can sit in a corner; pricing stays in your ad editor.

items.t: Batch Edit Product Photos
items.d: Every candle in the catalog can get the same linen surface. You do not open twelve files by hand.

items.t: Share Product Scenes With Your Team
items.d: Send the cafe scene to the person who owns the product page, before it goes live.

items.t: Save Logos, Fonts, and Brand Colors
items.d: Save the shop's mark and green you always use, so the next mug scene carries the same color.

items.t: Create a Simple Product Brand Mark

items.t: Edit Product Photos Across Devices
